planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Traviata is an early, disease-resilient Italian-type eggplant bred by Vitalis Organic Seeds and listed among Cornell's recommended disease-tolerant eggplant varieties, a useful trait for humid Gulf South gardens.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date, once nights stay reliably above 60°F; Traviata is an early-maturing, high-yielding Italian-type eggplant hybrid bred for vigor and improved disease resilience, producing a heavy, sustained crop of glossy, deep purple-black, oval fruit with few seeds and tender, mild flesh. Its early maturity lets Gulf Coast gardeners get a jump on the harvest before summer disease pressure builds, and the sturdy, well-branched plant continues setting fruit steadily through the season. Harvest while the skin is still glossy and the fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure, since dull skin signals overripe fruit with more seeds and a bitter edge. Keep soil consistently moist, since eggplant grown under drought stress develops tougher skin and a more bitter flavor.

common_name: Night Shadow Eggplant (Reliable Classic Black-Skinned Hybrid)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before transplanting; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Night Shadow is a Seminis-bred hybrid listed among Cornell's recommended disease-tolerant eggplant varieties, valued for its consistent yield and classic fruit quality.

directions: Set out transplants in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date, once nights stay reliably above 60°F; Night Shadow is a hybrid eggplant bred for reliable, sustained production of classic glossy black-purple, oval fruit on a sturdy, vigorous plant that tolerates the heat of a Gulf South summer well. It is listed among Cornell University's recommended disease-tolerant eggplant selections, giving it an edge in the humid, disease-prone conditions common across the Southeast. Harvest while the skin is still glossy and the fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure, since dull, hard fruit signals it has gone past peak quality and developed more seeds and bitterness. Keep soil consistently moist and pick regularly to encourage the plant to keep setting new fruit through the season.
sources: seed catalog reference (Stokes Seeds, Rupp Seeds, Seedway)
